memory_update.text: DT should remain a reference observability anchor for the AI/cloud control-plane node, but it is not the primary underfollowed discovery target.
SAIL is a newly re-public identity-governance candidate with a specific AI-agent identity product; verify whether agent and machine identity are material revenue drivers.

FROG maps to the AI software-supply-chain control plane through artifact management, model scanning, governance, and secure distribution across hybrid environments.

HashiCorp and CyberArk fit the node strongly but were excluded as standalone candidates because HashiCorp was acquired by IBM and CyberArk was acquired by Palo Alto Networks; they remain useful private/absorbed comparables for the control-plane thesis.

node: AI security, observability, data governance, and automation control-plane software
summary: Expanded the node with a two-lane universe focused on AI-era control-plane software. Dynatrace is included as the reference observability platform because it directly maps to AI/cloud workload monitoring. The underfollowed lane favors companies that are not usually marketed as headline AI beneficiaries but could become gating tools for production AI: SailPoint for agent and machine identity governance, Varonis for sensitive-data exposure and AI data security, and JFrog for AI/software supply-chain artifact governance. All candidates require later-layer verification that AI-related product language is translating into revenue, retention, workload usage, or customer expansion rather than AI-washing.
